results.title: Cloud Pricing Goes Dynamic — The Without Surprise Blog
results.author: Timothy O’Brien
highlights:
Cloud prices are moving again, and the movement looks like a change in the pricing regime rather than a run of one-off adjustments. Between September 17 and October 1, Nebius told customers that on-demand GPU rates would rise roughly 17 to 21 percent and memory-backed capacity about 41 percent, effective October 1. 1 2 OVHcloud unbundled local storage and public IPv4 addresses from its Public Cloud instances on the same date, which moved the price of an identical configuration up 1.4 to 21.9 percent depending on size. 3 CoreWeave announced that it has continued to contract new compute capacity at higher prices, on short terms of roughly three to six months. 4 Under all three announcements sits the same pressure: memory. TrendForce’s September 30 survey projects conventional DRAM contract prices up another 10 to 15 percent in the fourth quarter, after a year of much larger increases, with server DRAM undersupplied into 2027. 5

...

## What changed in the last month

Nebius notified customers on September 17 rather than issuing a press release: new on-demand rates take effect October 1. 1 The increases step up by chip generation, about 17 percent on H100 instances, 20 percent on H200, 19 percent on B200, 21 percent on the newest B300s, with AMD CPU rates up about 25 percent and memory-backed instances up roughly 41 percent, the largest single line in the notice. It was the company’s second increase in roughly three months. 2 The stock market read the notice as pricing power rather than distress: Nebius shares climbed about 10 percent that morning, and operators that had sent no note at all caught a bid alongside it. 6 The detail to notice is the memory line. Providers bundle memory into instance pricing, so it rarely appears on its own on a bill. A 41 percent increase on the memory line says the component inside every instance is repricing, not just the scarce GPUs on top.

OVHcloud did not raise an instance rate at all. What changed on October 1 is what the price includes. Local storage and ... IPv4 addresses, previously bundled with Generation 3 instances, became separate billing lines, about €10 ... per ter ... -month for ... and about €1. ... per ... for an address, and the ... for an identical configuration ... . ... 2 ... .9 ... : ... b ... -8 went ... €37 ... €45 ... month ... 3- ... from ... 33 ... 4 ... . 3 The company also replaced its Savings Plans grid, cutting terms to 12 or 36 months at 15 and 30 percent discounts, where the old grid had offered 35 percent on a 12-month commitment. Customers already inside a plan keep their guaranteed compute rate until the end of the commitment, but from October 1 the storage and address lines bill at full price, outside the guarantee.

results.title: Nebius GPU Price Hike: H100 to B300 Cloud Prices Rise | metir Blog
results.author: Metir AI Team
highlights:
Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices up to 21% on October 1, 2026, its second hike in months. What H100 to B300 cloud prices say about AI compute costs.

...

On October 1, 2026, the Nebius GPU price hike took effect: the neocloud raised on-demand rates for Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 instances by roughly 17% to 21%. Nebius's own pricing page now lists the new rates with that effective date and notes that prices exclude taxes and may change at any time (Nebius pricing). It is the second increase in a few months, and it runs against the story most people remember from 2024 and 2025, when GPU rental prices mostly fell.

$3.85 to $4.50 H100 per GPU-hour (+17%)

$4.50 to $5.40 H200 per GPU-hour (+20%)

$7.15 to $8.50 B200 per GPU-hour (+19%)

$7.85 to $9.50 B300 per GPU-hour (+21%)

NVIDIA

AMD

The hike covers Nvidia GPU instances and AMD EPYC Genoa CPU capacity.

...

Nebius's pricing page lists these on-demand rates per GPU-hour, before and from October 1: H100 $3.85 to $4.50, H200 $4.50 to $5.40, B200 $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 $7.85 to $9.50 (Nebius pricing). Our arithmetic on those figures gives 16.9%, 20.0%, 18.9% and 21.0%, matching press coverage.

...

The increase is not limited to GPUs. Stocktwits, citing a notice to customers, reports that AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU pricing rose from $0.012 to $0.015 per vCPU-hour (25%) and Genoa memory from $0.0032 to $0.0045 per GiB-hour (about 41%) (Stocktwits). Silicon UK adds that customers who reserve large clusters for several months can still receive discounts, and that the cumulative B300 increase across the two hikes is 56% (Silicon UK).

The earlier move came in May 2026. Yahoo Finance reported that Nebius would lift on-demand H100 rates from $2.95 to $3.85 per hour, about 29%, and that preemptible capacity rose 51% (Yahoo Finance). Put together, an H100 hour that cost $2.95 in spring costs $4.50 today, a rise of about 53% by our arithmetic.

### A note on confirmation

Early coverage disagreed about sourcing. Stocktwits said the details came from Nebius's communication to customers, reshared on Reddit and X, with no official public statement in its report. Silicon UK treated the rates as a Nebius announcement. The question is now largely settled by the company's own pricing page, which shows the October 1 rates. The two reports also differ slightly on timing: Stocktwits was published late on September 16, while Silicon UK dated its report September 18 and said Nebius announced the change "on Thursday."

results.title: Nebius raises prices across the board on… · Slicast
highlights:
# Nebius raises prices across the board on October 1: H100 +17% to $4.50/hour, B300 to $9.50/hour

...

N ebius, the Amsterdam-based neocloud provider, notified customers on September 17, 2026 that it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for Nvidia GPU instances, AMD CPU capacity, and memory starting October 1, 2026. It's the company's second price hike in three months, and this time the increases stretch well beyond GPUs into the CPU and memory tiers that most cloud budgets treat as an afterthought.

The numbers are specific. Nvidia H100 instances rise roughly 17% to $4.50 per GPU-hour from $3.85, H200 climbs 20% to $5.40 from $4.50, B200 goes up about 19% to $8.50 from $7.15, and the newest B300 chips take the biggest hit at 21%, reaching $9.50 per GPU-hour from $7.85. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rates jump 25%, and memory pricing rises about 41%, the steepest increase across the board. Investors read it as a sign of tight capacity, not weak demand: Nebius shares (Nasdaq: NBIS) jumped as much as 11.1% in pre-market trading the same day.

...

This is not an isolated move. Around May 2026, Nebius already raised on-demand capacity prices by an average of 29% and spot capacity by 51%. That means Nebius has now raised prices twice in under half a year, with the spring spot-market increase actually exceeding the September GPU hikes in percentage terms. Reuters framed the September move plainly: Nebius is raising prices because demand for computing power keeps rising faster than supply. It's closer to basic capacity rationing, the same mechanism that pushed cloud GPU rental rates up during the original 2023 H100 shortage, except this time it's spreading into CPU and memory tiers that used to be treated as commodity add-ons.

...

Cloud GPU pricing is notoriously hard to compare directly because providers mix spot, on-demand, reserved, and multi-year contract rates on the same public price list. But looking at H100 rental rates across the market as of September 2026 shows just how wide the spread is. ... Nebius now sits at $4.50 from October 1, CoreWeave at $4.25–$6.16 on-demand, and AWS's P5 instance pricing approaches $6.88 per GPU on a list-price basis. Nebius's increase moves it higher on the ladder but still below legacy hyperscalers, maintaining its position as a specialist provider with more capacity allocation and tighter pricing than the market leaders.

results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

The transaction side moved on its own path. OCPI for H200 went from $4.84 on September 28 to $5.57 on October 4. Over the same stretch, the lowest H200 list price we track held at $4.29 (Crusoe). List prices and transaction prices measure different things, and this week the gap between them widened. If you buy on-demand capacity from a Neocloud, posted price notices are worth tracking. This one landed on schedule, to the cent.

...

These are public catalog list prices, not live quotes, and a listing does not establish capacity or orderability.

The clearest evidence comes from providers themselves. Nebius disclosed its October 1 card through customer communications reshared on Reddit and X. H100 hourly rates rose about 17% to $4.50, H200 rose 20% to $5.40, B200 nearly 19% to $8.50, and B300 about 21% to $9.50 from $7.85. CPU pricing moved too, with AMD (AMD) EPYC Genoa climbing 25% to $0.015 per vCPU-hour and Genoa memory up roughly 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour. results.title: 再涨20％：GPU租金二度上调，算力缺口仍在拉大 - 与非网
results.author: 作者： 证券之星
highlights:
9月中旬，云计算服务提供商Nebius向客户发出调价通知，拟自10月1日起上调主要英伟达 GPU的按需(on-demand)租金：H100由每小时3.85美元升至4.50美元，H200由4.50美元升至5.40美元，B200由7.15美元升至8.50美元，B300由7.85美元升至9.50美元，本轮涨幅约17%至21%。

这已是该公司年内第二次全面上调按需价格。若按两轮公开报价计算，以其首轮调价前的6.10美元为起点，B300每小时租金年内累计涨幅已达约56%。

...

本轮调价并非孤立事件。今年5月宣布、6月1日生效的一轮提价中，Nebius已将H100由2.95美元/小时升至3.85美元，H200由3.50美元升至4.50美元，B200由5.50美元升至7.15美元，B300由6.10美元升至7.85美元，整体涨幅约29%。两轮叠加，Nebius自身报价序列的绝对水平因此被逐轮抬升。
